Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to

IS 1 595 -1954 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

BLOWN RAPE (OR MUSTARD) OIL FOR 

USE IN LUBRICANTS 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Insti* 
tution on 13 September 1954, on the joint endorsement by the Chemical 
Division Council and the Engineering Division Council of the draft final* 
ized on 23 April 1954, by the Lubricants Sectional Committee. 

0*2 It is well known that the addition of vegetable oils to mineral lubri- 
cating oils improves the oiliness, increases the viscosity index and reduces 
coefficient of frictioq. Rape ( or mustard ) oils after blowing are gene- 
rally added to straight mineral oils for better performance in the machi- 
nery in which such oils are used as lubricants. 

03 Taking into consideration the views of the producers, consumers and 
technologists, the Sectional Committee responsible for the preparation or 
this standard felt that it should be related to the existing trade practices in 
the country in this field. This consideration led the Committee to base 
this standard on: (i) the experimental data collected at the University 
Chemical Laboratories, Lahore, during 1936-41 while executing the 
scheme of Messrs Steel Bros, London; and (ii) data available with the 
Harcourt Butler Technological Institute, Kanpur; and with various oil 
companies. 

0.4 * Indian Standard Methods of Test for Petroleum and its Products * 
(IS : 1448 ( Part I )-1960 and IS : 1448 ( Part III )-1963 1 and ' Indian 
Standard Methods of Sampling and Test for Oils and Fats ( Revised ) ' 
( IS : 548-1964 ) are necessary adjuncts to this specification. 

0.4.1 Wherever a reference to any standard mentioned under 0.4 appears 
in this specification, it shall be taken as a reference to the latest version 
of the standard. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express* 
ing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
•IS: 2-1949 Rules for Rounding Off Numerical Values; the number of 
places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the 
specified value in this standard. 



ISt 595- 1954 

0.6 Thil standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions 
relating to the supply of the material, and it does not include all the 
necessary provisions of a contract. 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of test for 
blown rape ( or mustard ) oil, intended for compounding with various 
straight mineral lubricating oils. 

2. SAMPLING 

2.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed 
in IS : 1447*1966 ' Methods of Sampling of Petroleum and its Products \ 

S. REQUIREMENTS 

3.1 Description — The material shall be prepared from genuine and 
good quality rape ( or mustard ) oil. It shall be clear, homogeneous and 
free from any suspended matter, water, dirt and other visible impurities. 

3.2 The material shall comply with the requirements given in Table I. 
TABLE I REQUIREMENTS FOR BLOWN RAPE ( OR MUSTARD) OIL

4. TESTS 

4.1 Tests shall be carried out according to the methods prescribed in 
« Methods of Test for Petroleum and its Products * [ IS : 1448 ( Part I )-1960 
and IS : 1448 ( Part III )-1963 ], and ' Methods of Sampling and Test for 
Oils and Fats {Revised y ( IS : 548-1964 ). References to relevant teat 
methods and clause number are given in col 4, 5 and 6 of Table I.
